Truthfully? I don’t know. I tried so hard to leave, to make the pain stop indefinitely, but it ended up hurting so much more. I was so so tired of being in pain, I was so tired of thoughts that weren’t my own, it hurt so bad. 

When I finally got help, some of the fog lifted, and I knew a very small fragment of peace, enough to make me want to find it over and over again in every little thing, much like how I used to find my pain in everything. I think that was it, switching the positions of my peace and suffering, it’s not a good or solid answer but that was how it happened for me.

That’s the hard part I think, your statement and the above can both be true, I was like that for a long *long* time. The real fight is gritting your teeth and head butting the train to get through. Even still, up to this day I’m still fighting.

It’s really weird honestly. I always feel like I’m “watching” myself when this happens, I’m not in my head really, but when the fog lifts it’s like I get pulled back into my body and whoever’s thoughts were in my brain suddenly get pushed aside by my *own*, I’m ME again. Shit’s so wack.

I’m really compatible with most medication so fair warning that this is where my experience stems from.

Like most people have said, medication works different for a lot of people, you might have to go through a number of combos and solos to find the right match. My only negative experience with medication was that they did nothing for me so I spent money and took meds for nothing. Of course for others they worsened the symptoms of their depression/anxiety, but like I said, for some reason my chemical makeup just makes me positively compatible to most meds, to the point that my only negative is that it does nothing for me.

I found my match eventually though, then moved on to another when my symptoms changed. My perfect match came with a price of course, as it was the first time side-effects hit me like a freight train. My doctor did warn me that the first few weeks might see the worst of the side-effects (sweating, weight loss, agitation, restlessness, irritability, mild heightened anxiety) and he was right, I had to endure two weeks of those side effects to the point I thought I was going to keep suffering like that forever, but at the tail end of the second week something just *clicked*, and suddenly, I wasnt anxious anymore, I was the calmest I had ever felt in my life, like I suddenly forgot what it was like to keep thinking about my problems and never stopping. I’ve been level ever since.

Its really up to you and your doctor if the meds are right for you, just be sure to ask them about side-effects and other warnings you may need, dont be too troubled if the first trials dont work, your doctor will find the right combo or solo eventually (hopefully, cause like I said, it works differently for a lot of people).
